key_insight: G-PINNs use a Gaussian spatial weighting of the PINN loss to automatically focus training on high-gradient regions, improving shock and discontinuity resolution in low-viscosity Burgers’ flows.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to capture moving or unknown shock locations in PDE-constrained models without manually specifying where the solution is steepest.
method: Gaussian-based spatially weighted loss over collocation points
Adaptive emphasis on regions with large PDE residuals / gradients
Autonomous detection and tracking of moving discontinuities
evidence_signal: In 1D low-viscosity Burgers’ tests (ν = 0.0005), the method reduced relative L2 error to about 13% for a stationary shock and 14% for a moving shock, versus 45% and 33% for standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on 1D Burgers’ shock problems, so robustness on higher-dimensional or more complex flow physics still needs validation.
paper_title: G-PINNs: Gaussian-based spatially weighted formulation for PINNs: 1D low-viscous Burgers
